mia: Quick heads-up — ran a smoke harness this morning comparing replay vs synthetic for the embed->rerank path. Short thread with raw findings and next steps.

raj: Awesome, drop the numbers?

mia: Summary first: replay shows ~2.4x higher p99 than synthetic for same avg RPS. p50/p95 line up closely. Looks like KV cold misses and large payload spikes in replay are the culprit.

noah: Do you mean KV cache miss rate or network egress of the payloads?

mia: KV miss rate. On replay we hit ~18% cold misses during bursts; synthetic (uniform) had ~3%. When we disable prefix caching in runtime, p99 falls back to synthetic levels, which implies cache priming behavior is critical.

perf-bot: Perf run summary uploaded: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/1831750123 (summary csv + flamegraphs) :rocket:

mia: Key figures from run: model=embed-512 / reranker-v2, vector dim=512, avg payload per request=3.2KB, max spike=27KB, batch config={max_batch:64, max_wait_ms:8}. Replay: RPS=250, p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=340ms. Synthetic (poisson): RPS=250, p50=48ms, p95=125ms, p99=140ms.

sasha: That's a big p99 gap. Kernel selection differences? Were kernels identical across runs?

mia: Yes, same kernel selection (auto) and same quant profile (int8 for embed, fp16 for rerank). But we forced kernel->single-thread fallback for large payloads and saw p99 drop by ~40ms — suggests IO/serialization path contention.

raj: Any signs of serialization blocking the event loop? Logs?

mia: Saw repeated log lines: "kv_cache: miss->backend_fetch latency=120ms" in replay bursts. Also worker queues hitting queue_depth ~60 (near max_batch).

noah: Could be batching heuristic: max_wait_ms=8 may let large requests coalesce and create stragglers. Try lowering max_batch to 32 or reduce max_wait to 4ms for sensitivity.

mia: Did quick test: max_batch=32, max_wait_ms=4 -> p99(replay)=210ms (from 340ms), throughput stable. Synthetic p99 unchanged. So batching was amplifying tail under replay.

sasha: Interesting. What's the impact of vector dim / payload size?

mia: Ran dimensional sweep: dims=[256,512,1024]. Larger dims increase per-token kernel time predictably; but the tail gap persisted proportionally. Payload spikes >20KB caused a separate spike due to gRPC frame splitting and additional memcpy.

raj: Any kernel-level notes? Did runtime switch kernels for large sequences?

mia: The kernel selector flips to the large-seq kernel when seq_len>1024; that path allocates a temporary KV buffer and does a memcpy. Under heavy concurrency those memcpys hit the same numa node and we saw 10-15% CPU steal in perf counters.

noah: So multiple factors: KV cold misses, batching heuristics that cause stragglers, and memcpy/NUMA effects on large payloads.

mia: Yep. Proposed follow-ups: 1) Update replay harness to inject realistic payload spikes (preserve original payload size distro). 2) Run long-run (1M reqs) replay with new harness to get stable p99. 3) Experiment with adaptive batching: cap batch size when payload_size > X. 4) Add async KV prefetch for top-K prefixes.

sasha: For (3) we could add a per-request 'payload_bytes' hint and let scheduler reduce batch target dynamically.

raj: Also add a synthetic workload that simulates KV miss cascades so synthetic better matches replay tail.

perf-bot: Created perf ticket PERF-2184 with run artifacts and flamegraphs: https://issues.redwood/2184

mia: I'll run the 1M replay later today with adaptive batching toggled. Posting the config here once queued.

noah: Nice. If you hit consistent repro, let's bisect kernel version (v2.3 vs v2.4) — we recently landed an allocator tweak that might interact with memcpy patterns.

mia: Good call. I'll include kernel version matrix in the run.

sasha: Thanks for the quick signal. Small ask: can we also log per-request "kv_hit_hint" in debug builds for a short window to validate prefetch heuristics?

mia: Will do.

raj: TL;DR for the ops doc: synthetic is fine for p50/p95 but underestimates p99 without payload-size spikes and KV miss behavior. Replay -> necessary for tail accuracy.

mia: Agreed. I'll add a short blurb to the benchmarking guide and attach the config diff.

perf-bot: run queued: id=run-1831751800, ETA ~35m

mia: Thanks all. Closing thread once long-run completes.

noah: :thumbsup:
